messages:
ravi: Heads-up — during the long-token prompt curation pass I noticed a fragmentation issue: many prompts that are semantically identical are split across different canonical IDs because of trailing context truncation. This is skewing our sampling and golden coverage.

claire: can you give an example?

ravi: example in s3: s3://redwood-internal/curation/longfrag/2026-03-18/examples.txt — two prompts that differ only by a trailing code block comment and our tokenizer splits them into different canonical hashes. Both map to different fingerprint buckets.

jose: is this tokenizer drift or prompt-preprocess inconsistency from ingestion?

ravi: looks like a mix: 40% ingestion normalization (newline vs space) and 60% long-token clipping where the suffix differs but intent identical. Impact: rare-intent recall drops in holdouts and dedupe erroneously keeps duplicates, which screws golden sampling.

claire: plan: we should run a normalization + suffix-collapse pass for long prompts (>4k tokens) before dedupe. Also surface a reranking step that groups by semantic cluster rather than raw fingerprint.

ravi: Agreed. I propose triage: 1) create a micro-bundle of 200 candidate pairs (high-similarity embedding but different fingerprints), 2) labeler triage to mark KEEP / MERGE / ALIAS, 3) update gold manifest with alias_of for MERGE, 4) update ingest preprocess to canonicalize trailing whitespace and code fences.

jose: for labeling, we need clear instructions: define MERGE = same user intent and interchangeable for evals; ALIAS = near-identical but prefer canonical id; KEEP = distinct. If labeler unsure, pick AMBIG and add note.

claire: also add a rule: for long prompts, when only suffix differs (like a long log tail or stack trace), prefer MERGE if core prompt intent is intact. We should surface the most common suffix tokens in the UI to help labelers.

labeler-bot: New job created: longfrag-curation-triage-20260318  200 tasks, redundancy=2. Link: https://labeling.redwood/jobs/longfrag-curation-triage-20260318

ravi: timeline: triage complete in 48h, golden adjudication in 24h after. We'll then apply alias mapping and reindex gold embeddings. If >3% of gold changes, block any scheduled model rollouts that depend on that gold set.

jose: small technical ask: store a compact suffix-fingerprint (last 256 tokens) in the sample metadata so we can detect suffix-only differences cheaply.

ops-bot: Feature flag created: ingest.canonicalize_long_suffix -> default on for canary. Rollout plan: canary -> prod if stable.

claire: also run the dedupe pipeline against quantized model embeddings (q4b,int4) to see if merge decisions differ by model variant. We don't want to accidentally over-merge because a quant variant collapses embeddings.

ravi: good call. I've added in the harness to compute embedding concordance across fp16 and quant variants during triage. Results will be attached to each pair.

labeler-bot: Job accepted by labeler-group: quick-gold. ETA: 2026-03-19T11:00Z.

jose: post-triage actions: generate mapping file s3://redwood-internal/curation/longfrag/mapping-20260318.json and run a dry-run apply that prefixes alias_of fields but does not mutate manifest until golden signoff.

claire: also add the newly merged canonical IDs to the golden refresh candidate list, we may want to promote some merged examples to the golden set if they increase coverage.

ravi: caution: do not promote blindly. We should only add items to golden after golden adjudication and a quick eval to ensure they don't change metric baselines.

labeler-bot: Quick update: 60/200 triage tasks completed. Current MERGE rate 28%, AMBIG 5%.

jose: MERGE 28% seems high on surfaced prefilter; good we human-triage. If final MERGE fraction >10% of the surfaced bundle we should run a secondary sweep on similar clusters to ensure we didn't miss systemic issues.

claire: final gate: if post-adjudication applied changes modify any onboarding eval metric by >1.5% (precision/recall on our holdouts), we pause the onboarding pipeline and run regression evaluations.

ravi: I'll add a small diagnostic that simulates the onboarding eval suite pre/post alias apply and reports deltas.

ops-bot: Reindex job queued: REINDEX-LONGFRAG-20260319. Expected completion: 2026-03-20T02:00Z.

labeler-bot: Golden adjudication job created for AMBIGs: 20 tasks, redundancy=3. Link: https://labeling.redwood/jobs/longfrag-golden-20260319

jose: follow-ups: patch ingestion docs with canonicalization rules, add unit tests to dedupe pipeline for suffix-collapse, and include suffix-fingerprint in sample metadata.

claire: tagging @labeling-team and @platform-ops — please prioritize the triage job if possible; this affects multiple onboards.

labeler-bot: Golden adjudication complete: 20/20 -> 6 KEEP, 10 MERGE, 4 DROP. Final mapping file uploaded to s3://redwood-internal/curation/longfrag/mapping-final-20260319.json

ravi: applied aliases in dry-run and ran onboarding eval diff: delta precision -0.3%, recall +0.4% -> within threshold. Proceeding to apply manifest changes and reindex.

jose: thanks. After reindex, let's run a 7-day rolling check to make sure no new fragmentation patterns appear and set an alert if fragmentation-prone clusters spike.

claire: added alert: curation.fragmentation.rate > 0.5% over baseline triggers pager for curation-oncall.

ravi: closing this loop — will post final manifest version here once reindex job completes. Thanks all. :rocket:
